globalAssumptions: Generated from the supplied data/sample_user_profiles.json content in the uploaded prompt file.

Only the first 10 complete profiles are returned because the full 50-profile utility patch would exceed practical single-response length; continueFromSampleUserId identifies the next profile to generate.
Annual utility period is 2025-06-01 through 2026-05-31, with monthly calendar periods from 2025-06 through 2026-05.
Synthetic masked account numbers are deterministic fixture values and are not actual private account numbers.
Annual usage and cost fields are computed from the monthly records, with average unit costs computed from annual cost divided by annual usage.

modelingNotes: Modeled as a 325,000-square-foot urban public school with classrooms, cafeteria, gym, auditorium, offices, and after-school/event use.
Electric use reflects school ventilation and cooling needs, IAQ-sensitive HVAC operation, lighting, plug loads, kitchen equipment, and summer maintenance schedules.
Gas is strongly winter-peaking for Boston heating, cafeteria hot water, and supplemental kitchen loads.
Water and sewer reflect school-year occupancy, cafeteria service, locker room and restroom use, and limited summer usage.
Waste includes school-day landfill, recycling, cafeteria organics, and event-related overages.
No source URLs were checked; values rely only on the supplied sample profile fields and the supplied estimated square footage.

modelingNotes: Modeled as a 100,000-square-foot five-story public university research and institutional building in Fairbanks.
Electric use is winter-biased because ventilation, lighting, research equipment, and cold-climate building systems sustain higher winter base loads despite limited cooling.
Gas is strongly winter-peaking for extreme-cold heating; utility-bill style values do not attempt to resolve potential district-heat metering complexity.
Water and sewer are moderate institutional loads from offices, research support, library-like functions, and restrooms, with little irrigation assumed.
Waste is office/research-support scale and excludes hazardous, laboratory, and regulated research waste categories from the generic waste fixture.
No source URLs were checked; values rely only on the supplied sample profile fields.

Gas is winter-peaking but moderate because high-performance envelope and systems reduce heating intensity compared with standard municipal buildings.
Water and sewer include office occupancy, emergency operations, public functions, custodial use, and some landscape irrigation.
Waste includes municipal office, secure-document, recycling, and event/civic-service streams, not law-enforcement evidence or regulated materials.
No source URLs were checked; values rely only on the supplied sample profile fields.

modelingNotes: Modeled as a tribal multi-utility headquarters and operations campus; square footage is unknown and a conservative 65,000-square-foot-equivalent office/operations baseline was inferred.
Electric use includes utility administration, customer service, operations support, telecommunications, dispatch-like functions, and field-service support spaces.
Gas is included because the supplied profile lists Navajo Tribal Utility Authority as gas provider; values are office/operations scale rather than distribution-system throughput.

Water and wastewater are included because the applicant is a multi-utility and the headquarters likely has office, operations, and landscape water loads; fixture values are site-use, not utility-system sales.
Waste includes office, operations, recycling, and limited yard/service debris streams, excluding regulated utility construction waste.
No source URLs were checked; values rely only on the supplied sample profile fields and an inferred headquarters/operations baseline.
